OXY.thesis_one_line: Low-cost Permian oil producer that just used a $9.7bn chemicals-unit sale to slash debt, backed by Warren Buffett's 34% stake.
kill_criteria: WTI averages below $55/bbl for two consecutive quarters (would break the reverse-DCF base case).
Consolidated long-term debt (noncurrent, per 10-Q) rises back above $18bn (reversal of the OxyChem-proceeds paydown).
Quarterly free cash flow (OCF minus capex) negative for two consecutive quarters (Q1 2026 was already negative once).
1PointFive/DAC capex exceeds $1.5bn in any fiscal year without matching signed offtake revenue disclosed.
Berkshire Hathaway stake falls below 20% (loss of the anchor-quality signal) or files to sell down materially.
key_adverse_facts: Q1 2026 free cash flow (OCF $1,281M minus capex $1,554M) was negative (-$273M), a real quarter-over-quarter deceleration versus Q1 2025.

GAAP net income is heavily distorted by a ~$3.1bn one-time after-tax gain on the OxyChem sale booked in discontinued operations in Q1 2026 only (Q2 2026 EPS of $2.75 is continuing operations at a $92.79 WTI average), plus recurring mark-to-market swings on Berkshire's warrants; headline EPS is not a clean operating signal.
1PointFive direct-air-capture remains pre-commercial-scale, cash-consuming, and unproven at scale despite a $500m DOE award.

Berkshire Hathaway holds warrants for 83.5m shares at a ~$59.62 strike (temporarily reduced to $21.30 for the publicly traded warrants per a March 2025 amendment) - a structural dilution/overhang risk if exercised.

Occidental has $8,287M of preferred stock (Berkshire) costing $680M a year in preferred dividends ($170M per quarter), a senior claim on cash flow that the FCF-yield valuation ignores; and the 6.66% FCF yield embeds roughly $93 WTI (Q2 2026) against a $60-70 base case. [Corrected 2026-10-08, DV32: added]
data_conflicts: Revenue jumped from $5,230M (Q1 2026) to $8,065M (Q2 2026) partly because OxyChem was deconsolidated 2 Jan 2026, making YoY/QoQ revenue comparisons across the deconsolidation boundary not like-for-like; the quant snapshot's NTM revenue growth figures likely embed this discontinuity and should not be read as organic growth.
OXY.confidence_in_thesis: medium - balance sheet deleveraging is filed fact and durable; oil-price and DAC-capital risk are real and outside the company's control

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No v1 row exists for OXY. The dossier's reverse DCF (6.7% FCF yield at ~9% cost of capital, 2-2.5% perpetual growth) used a yield that embeds Q2 2026 WTI of $92.79 while the base case is $60-70, and ignored $680M a year of preferred dividends. Normalised to the dossier's own base (FY2025 continuing OCF less capex less preferred, about $2.7bn; equity basis, market cap $56.8bn, ten years then 3%) the implied 10-year FCF growth is 4.5% (Ke 8.5%) to 6.3% (Ke 9.3%), in line with a mid-single-digit base. Verdict INCLUDE-SMALL unchanged.

OXY.scenario_basis: Base: FCF yield 6.7% at $56.86 close, ~3% FCF/production growth, modest multiple re-rating as leverage falls, 1.9% dividend maintained; bear: WTI sustained near $50 compresses FCF yield and multiple; bull: WTI $75+ plus DAC optionality re-rates the stock toward peer E&P multiples.

P.thesis_one_line: Fast-growing enterprise flash-storage maker winning hyperscaler AI deals, but its cash flow just turned negative and the stock is priced for a turnaround that has not shown up yet.
kill_criteria: Free cash flow (OCF minus capex) remains negative in the Q3 FY2027 10-Q (quarter ending approximately November 2026).
FY2027 full-year free cash flow comes in below $500m (versus the $600-800m guided range) when reported at the FY2027 10-K.
Any single customer/hyperscaler reappears above 10% of revenue or receivables in a 10-Q/10-K.
Cash and equivalents fall below $250m in any quarter without a corresponding revolver draw or financing disclosed.
Revenue growth decelerates below 25% YoY for two consecutive quarters.
key_adverse_facts: Q2 FY2027 (quarter ended 2 Aug 2026) free cash flow was approximately -$237.6M (OCF -$136.3M, capex $101.3M), confirmed by SEC XBRL differencing and by the company's 26-Aug-2026 release (free cash flow $(238)M); Q1 FY27 free cash flow was positive (+$112M), so only one quarter is negative.
Cash and equivalents fell from $854.9M (1 Feb 2026) to $385.7M (2 Aug 2026); including $622.2M of marketable securities, total liquidity fell about 35%, from ~$1.5bn to $1.0bn.
Trailing GAAP P/E is 172.6x and trailing FCF yield is negative, meaning there is essentially no valuation cushion if the promised H2 FY2027 cash-flow inflection slips.
Sizeable insider selling by CEO Charles Giancarlo (~$11m) and founder John Colgrove (~$17m) in the past year, with no offsetting insider buying reported.
data_conflicts: The Q12 triage card's characterization of 'negative FCF yield (-0.3%)' understates the severity found in the filings: the single most recent quarter's FCF was approximately -$237.6M, not a marginal, near-zero figure.
P.confidence_in_thesis: low - the bull case depends entirely on an unconfirmed H2 FY2027 free-cash-flow guidance promise that has not yet been delivered in a filed quarter

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No v1 row exists for P (or PSTG) in v1_valuation_table.csv/v1_valuation.json, so v1_verdict is null. My own reverse-DCF read is that a negative trailing FCF yield plus a 6.3x EV/Sales multiple prices in an FCF turnaround as near-certain (the $600-800m FY2027 FCF figure does not appear in the Q4 FY26, Q1 FY27 or Q2 FY27 releases and is unverified); that is a higher bar than my base case, which only credits the growth as proven, not yet the cash conversion, hence 'expensive' rather than 'fair'. Verification DV32 (2026-10-08): no discount rate or growth number had been computed; on a TTM FCF-after-SBC basis (about -$420M) the call implied_vs_base = above stands.

P.scenario_basis: Base: revenue growth decelerates from ~38% to the mid-teens by year 3 as hyperscaler ramp matures, FCF margin normalizes to ~12-15%, modest de-rating from 33.9x NTM P/E; bear: FCF turnaround fails to materialize, multiple compresses toward hardware-peer levels; bull: FCF turnaround delivers as guided and hyperscaler design wins expand, supporting continued premium multiple.

PANW.thesis_one_line: Leading cybersecurity platform bundling network, cloud and identity security after a $25 billion acquisition, but priced at nearly 100 times forward earnings after a GAAP loss quarter.
kill_criteria: Adjusted free-cash-flow margin fails to reach at least approximately 30% by FY2028 (halfway to the 40% target) as an interim checkpoint at the FY2027 10-K.
GAAP operating income is negative for two or more quarters in the next four (versus the single Q3 FY2026 loss so far).
Next-Gen Security ARR growth decelerates below 40% YoY for two consecutive quarters.
Any disclosed goodwill impairment related to CyberArk or Chronosphere in a future 10-K/10-Q.
NTM P/E remains above 70x while GAAP net margin stays below 5% for three consecutive quarters.
key_adverse_facts: Q3 FY2026 (quarter ended 30 Apr 2026) GAAP operating income and net income were both negative (-$183M and -$177M respectively) and Q4 FY2026 GAAP net income was again negative (-$282M, operating income +$172M), driven by CyberArk/Chronosphere acquisition costs and purchase-accounting amortization.

The CyberArk deal issued approximately 112 million new shares (plus $2.3bn cash), a real, permanent dilution event; stockholders' equity nearly tripled from $9.4bn to $27.5bn largely via share issuance, not retained earnings.
FY2026 full-year GAAP net income was only $307M on $11.48bn revenue (2.7% net margin), while the stock trades at 76.8-96.6x NTM P/E - an extreme GAAP-to-multiple disconnect.

Headline revenue growth (+31% in Q3 FY2026) is partly acquisition-driven ($388M of $3.0bn came directly from CyberArk/Chronosphere), overstating organic momentum versus the ~60% NGS-ARR growth figure, which itself includes $1.6bn of acquired ARR; FY27 company guidance is only +23-24% revenue growth (Q4 FY26 release, 1-Sep-2026).
data_conflicts: Q2 FY2026 YoY revenue growth (+15%) looks anomalously low compared to the +25% (Q1 FY2026) and +31% (Q3 FY2026) figures either side of it; likely a prior-year comparative-base artifact rather than a genuine deceleration, but not fully resolved in this pass.
d4 quant snapshot shows two different NTM P/E calculations for PANW (76.8x and 96.6x) depending on method; both are cited in the dossier rather than reconciled to one number.
PANW.confidence_in_thesis: medium - the GAAP loss and dilution are filed facts, but whether the valuation ever reconverges to fundamentals depends on multi-year integration execution not yet provable from two quarters of data

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No v1 row exists for PANW. The dossier's qualitative multiple (40% FY28 adjusted FCF margin, ~48x forward FCF at a $318bn EV) used adjusted FCF with SBC added back and an EV that ignored $5.4bn of investments (EV is ~$300bn). On the programme basis (equity basis, market cap $306.5bn, FY26 FCF after SBC ~$2.3bn, Ke 8.1-10.3%, ten years then 3%) the implied 10-year FCF growth is 27-34%, far above any defensible base case; implied_vs_base = above is confirmed. FY27 guidance is revenue $14.10-14.20bn (+23-24%) and adjusted FCF margin 38.0%.

PANW.scenario_basis: Base: organic (NGS ARR) growth decelerates from 60% toward the high-20s/low-30s as CyberArk laps, adjusted FCF margin advances toward but does not fully reach the 40% FY28 target, multiple compresses from ~77-97x NTM toward the 40-50x range; bear: integration stumbles, GAAP losses persist, multiple compresses sharply; bull: integration succeeds ahead of schedule, cross-sell drives durable 30%+ growth and margin expansion, supporting a still-rich multiple.
